learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how India uses its land, the changing face of farming, and the crops that feed over a billion people!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Land is classified by the government into categories like Forests, Barren/Wasteland, Land put to non-agricultural uses (cities/roads), Pastures, Fallow lands, and Net Sown Area (where crops are actually grown).
As the economy grows, land shifts from agriculture to non-agricultural uses (building factories and cities). The proportion of agricultural land is under intense pressure.
India has three main agricultural seasons: Kharif (Monsoon season: Rice, Cotton), Rabi (Winter season: Wheat, Gram), and Zaid (Short summer season: Watermelon, Vegetables).

Farming depends on moisture availability. It can be Irrigated farming (protective or productive) or Rainfed farming (dryland farming for drought-resistant crops, or wetland farming in high rainfall areas).
Despite the Green Revolution, farmers face massive challenges like dependence on erratic monsoons, fragmented landholdings, lack of commercialization, degradation of soil, and debt.

fun_activity.title: 🍽️ The Seasonal Plate
fun_activity.instructions: Look at your dinner tonight. Try to identify whether the main ingredients (like wheat chapati or rice) are Kharif or Rabi crops! Wheat is a winter (Rabi) crop, while Rice needs a lot of water (Kharif).

exam_tips: 📌 Learn the formula for Cropping Intensity: (Gross Cropped Area ÷ Net Sown Area) × 100.
📌 Distinguish between Dryland farming (conserving soil moisture) and Wetland farming (dealing with excess water).
📌 Be prepared to list the major problems of Indian agriculture and suggest sustainable solutions.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Net Sown Area' is the physical extent of land on which crops are sown and harvested.
⭐ The Green Revolution (introduction of High Yielding Variety seeds) dramatically increased wheat and rice production in Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP.
⭐ Common Property Resources (CPRs) like village pastures are crucial for the livelihood of landless and marginal farmers.
